Biography Overview
The Bateau-Lavoir in Montmartre, Paris
Otto Freundlich

Le Bateau-Lavoir (the laundry-boat) was the name given to a block of ramshackle, one-story buildings at 13 Rue Ravignan (Place Emile Goudeau), in the Montmartre section of Paris. Artists first settled there in the 1890's, but the best-known arrived between 1902 and 1904. Picasso is reputed to have invented cubism at the Bateau-Lavoir.


The bateau-lavoir in mid-twentieth century
.

In 1908, when Freundlich shared a studio there with Reverdy and Wiegels, several other artists had studios in the same block. One studio was shared by Picasso and Herbin, another by Gris, Van Dongen, and Vallant, and another by Favereau and Patureau.


Another relatively recent (rear) view of the Bateau-Lavoir
.

In addition to the artists who actually lived in the Bateau- Lavoir, there were many who frequented the place, or gathered in nearby cafés. Most of the artists left the Bateau-Lavoir in 1914, after the outbreak of the First World War. The building was destroyed by fire in 1970.


The Bateau-Lavoir (upper right) circa 1900.
